findings: Promise.all required both the dancer and portrait before opening either window.
No application API 5xx or slow HTTP requests appear in the collected production request logs; both jobs succeeded.

Opening microphone incremented generationEpoch, silently discarding pending results even if the recording failed or was empty. This is a possible cancellation mechanism, not proven to be the incident cause.
One failed job-poll fetch aborted the wait without reconnecting.
Generation exceptions were stored in memory but not emitted to Cloud Logging; no client cancellation/error telemetry existed.
uncertainty: The original reason the browser stopped polling at ~39 seconds is not recoverable from existing server logs. It could be cancellation, navigation or a client-side network failure. Do not claim a confirmed infrastructure timeout.
fixes: Render Celery/Oyster primary dancer as soon as ready; add portrait independently when ready and only if its original dancer still exists.
Keep portrait errors visible without withholding the dancer.
Retry only read-only job polling for transient network errors/timeouts and HTTP 502/503/504, bounded to three attempts.
Surface non-JSON gateway errors as readable HTTP failures; never automatically repeat generation POST.
Do not cancel generation merely on microphone opening.
Emit generation start/settled/error and request failure logs to Cloud Logging and local JSONL; record browser generation ready/error/cancelled events.

browserFaultInjection: Injected a 504 on the second portrait poll; primary video remained playing and polling recovered.
Held portrait working; primary video paused=false, readyState=4.
Released portrait complete; both videos paused=false, readyState=4.
Forced portrait timeout; persistent Portrait unavailable message and primary video paused=false, readyState=4.
validation.note: Browser fault injection used original local video fixtures, no new model generation. Production deployment was not changed.
